correctness.rationale: For the scaled masses \(p_n\), the identity \(P_k(z)=\exp(\lambda\sum_{j=1}^kz^j)\) and the untruncated \(Q(z)=\exp(\lambda z/(1-z))\) give exact differences \(p_{k+2+t}-p_{k+1+t}=\lambda^2(S_{k+t}-T_t)\) for \(0\le t\le k-2\). Vandermonde convolution and \((i+j+2)!\ge(i+1)!(j+2)!\) yield \(S_{k+t}\le S_kT_t\). For rates below the unique positive root of \(S_k=1\), the entire interior first block decreases. The missing \(p_k>p_{k+1}\) edge is proved for \(k\ge3\) via root \(<1\) and separately at \(k=2\) using \(r=2(\sqrt7-2)>6/5\). The recurrence \(np_n=\lambda\sum_{j=1}^k j p_{n-j}\) propagates strict descent to all later indices. Conversely \(p_{k+2}-p_{k+1}=\lambda^2(S_k-1)\) obstructs all rates at or above the root. All quantifiers, normalizing factors, and endpoint conditions are covered. A newly extracted standalone checker corroborates 504 exact finite identities/comparisons, not the infinite quantifier.

value.rationale: This settles Mane 2023b Conjecture 4.3 for every integer order using a sharp necessary-and-sufficient condition for an infinite sequence of mass inequalities. The object is a standard uniform-jump compound Poisson distribution. A local polynomial threshold rigorously controls the global tail shape, relevant to mode/tail analysis. The result is not an arbitrary numerical cutoff, a routine corollary of the prior conditional induction, or an order-specific calculation.
